By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: High-coherence multimode mechanical resonators are crucial for quantum information processing, but loss mechanisms limit their performance. Understanding and mitigating these losses is essential for advancing hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors systematically study loss mechanisms in bulk acoustic resonators, optimizing the piezoelectric transducer's properties. They likely use experimental characterization and materials analysis to identify and reduce sources of dissipation.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics, providing guidelines for future device design.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that careful optimization of piezoelectric transducers can significantly enhance the performance of mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, exploiting high-spin nuclei for qudit encoding.
result: Demonstrates a universal approach for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, which is essential for higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme paves the way for realizing higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during transmon readout limit qubit fidelity, and the authors aim to mitigate this by engineering the readout coupling.
method: They employ a cosφ coupling element in the transmon readout circuit and perform experimental measurements alongside numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The proposed cosφ coupling is an effective approach to enhance transmon readout fidelity, relevant for quantum computing hardware.

title: Higher-form Entanglement Asymmetry And Topological Order
authors: Amanda Gatto Lamas, Jacopo Gliozzi, And Taylor L. Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Amanda Gatto Lamas, Jacopo Gliozzi, and Taylor L. Hughes

We extend a recently defined measure of symmetry breaking, the entanglement asymmetry, to higher-form symmetries. In particular, we focus on Abelian topological order in two dimensions, which spontaneously breaks a 1-form symmetry. Using the toric code as a primary example, we compute the entangleme…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105119] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the entanglement asymmetry measure to higher-form symmetries, using the toric code to compute it for 1-form symmetry breaking in 2D topological order.
motivation: To generalize a recently defined measure of symmetry breaking (entanglement asymmetry) to higher-form symmetries, which are relevant for topological order.
method: The authors define the higher-form entanglement asymmetry and compute it for the toric code, a paradigmatic example of 2D Abelian topological order that spontaneously breaks a 1-form symmetry.
result: They obtain explicit results for the entanglement asymmetry in the toric code, demonstrating its behavior and connection to topological order.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for characterizing symmetry breaking in topological phases, potentially useful for detecting and quantifying topological order.

title: Highly Robust Logical Qubit Encoding In An Ensemble Of V-symmetrical Qutrits
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, And Julio Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, and Julio Guerrero

We propose using even and odd Schrödinger cat states formed from coherent states of U(3) of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration (a qubit-disguised qutrit) to encode a logical qubit. These carefully engineered logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033169] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes encoding a logical qubit in even and odd Schrödinger cat states of U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of V-symmetrical qutrits, demonstrating robust, parameter-independent stationary states.
motivation: To find robust encodings of logical qubits that are resilient to parameter variations and decoherence, leveraging the structure of qutrit ensembles.
method: The authors construct even and odd cat states from U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of qutrits with V symmetry, and analyze their properties as logical qubit encodings.
result: The proposed logical qubit states are stationary and parameter-independent, offering robustness against certain errors, and the encoding is shown to be feasible in an ensemble of qutrits.
conclusion: The work provides a novel approach to logical qubit encoding using qutrit ensembles, with potential applications in quantum information processing and error mitigation.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature properties, such as extensive entanglement, challenging conventional notions of ground states.
motivation: To explore the possibility of realizing infinite-temperature-like properties in ground states of local Hamiltonians, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors construct specific local Hamiltonians and analyze their ground states, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to demonstrate extensive entanglement and other infinite-temperature characteristics.
result: They show that ground states can inherit infinite-temperature properties, including extensive entanglement, which is typically associated with high-energy states.
conclusion: The findings suggest that ground states of local Hamiltonians can exhibit thermal-like properties, offering new insights into the interplay between quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum computational advantage in a programmable ultracold-atom processor, which is a key goal in quantum information processing.
method: The authors use an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as digital quantum simulation or analog simulation with controlled interactions.
result: The processor exhibits a quantum computational advantage, showing that it can perform a task that is intractable for classical computers, as evidenced by the simulation of highly entangled dynamics.
conclusion: This work provides a concrete demonstration of quantum computational advantage in a scalable platform, advancing the field of quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent time evolution simulation, which achieves better query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus than gradient-descent methods.
motivation: Quantum optimization often suffers from barren plateaus and high query complexity in gradient-based approaches. The authors aim to develop a more efficient and robust optimization strategy.
method: They introduce a gradient-free approach that simulates time evolution to explore the parameter space, avoiding direct gradient computations. The method is analyzed theoretically and compared with gradient-descent-based methods.
result: The proposed method demonstrates improved query complexity and resilience to barren plateaus, as shown through theoretical analysis and numerical experiments.
conclusion: The gradient-free dynamical simulation approach offers a promising alternative for quantum optimization, potentially enhancing the practicality of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in continual quantum learning, showing that quantum neural networks maintain adaptability as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, while quantum neural networks may offer inherent advantages in retaining plasticity.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, comparing plasticity retention with classical counterparts.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, avoiding catastrophic forgetting even as the number of parameters increases.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks could provide a robust framework for continual learning, with implications for quantum machine learning and adaptive quantum information processing.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements or demand massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time operation, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for quantum error correction, potentially enabling real-time correction in future quantum computers.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for benchmarking quantum advantage experiments.
method: The authors analyze the statistical properties of output probabilities of random circuits under depolarizing noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They identify distinct depth-dependent regimes where anticoncentration is either achieved, degraded, or completely lost, and show that the behavior is universal across different circuit architectures.
conclusion: The findings provide a comprehensive framework for predicting when noisy quantum circuits can exhibit anticoncentration, which is essential for practical quantum information processing and for validating quantum supremacy claims.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity has been lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states required to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank dictates the minimum resources for preparing, compressing, and measuring non-Gaussian states, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a powerful tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential applications in quantum computing.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. The authors aim to demonstrate a quantum advantage for a practical problem, potentially driving new applications.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and amplitude estimation to compute persistence diagrams, achieving exponential speedup over classical methods under certain conditions.
result: The algorithm provides provable quantum speedups for computing persistence in TDA, with rigorous complexity analysis showing exponential improvement in relevant parameters.
conclusion: The work establishes a clear quantum advantage for a concrete data analysis task, highlighting the potential of quantum computing in practical applications beyond cryptography and simulation.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Sampling Of Pauli Strings For Nonstabilizerness
authors: Zhenyu Xiao And Shinsei Ryu

Quantum magic, quantified by nonstabilizerness, measures departures from stabilizer structure and underlies potential quantum speedups. We introduce an efficient classical framework for computing stabilizer Rényi entropies and stabilizer nullity of generic [MATH]-qubit wave functions. The method combin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070402] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient classical framework for computing stabilizer Rényi entropies and stabilizer nullity, exponentially accelerating the sampling of Pauli strings for nonstabilizerness quantification.
motivation: Quantum magic (nonstabilizerness) is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its computation is often inefficient. The authors aim to provide a scalable classical method to compute these measures for generic many-qubit states.
method: The method combines classical simulation techniques with efficient sampling of Pauli strings, likely using Monte Carlo or tensor network approaches, to estimate stabilizer Rényi entropies and nullity.
result: The framework achieves exponential acceleration in sampling Pauli strings, enabling computation of nonstabilizerness for larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantifying quantum magic, which is relevant to quantum information theory and resource theories.

title: Equivalence Between Exponential Concentration In Quantum Machine Learning Kernels And Barren Plateaus In Variational Algorithms
authors: Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, And Roman V. Krems
abstract:
Author(s): Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, and Roman V. Krems

We show that a parametrized quantum neural network can be used to build a nonparametric quantum kernel for machine learning that inherits the concentration properties of the neural network cost function. This construction establishes a rigorous connection between barren plateaus (BPs) in variational…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022417] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, linking two important phenomena in quantum computing.
motivation: Barren plateaus hinder the trainability of variational quantum algorithms, and exponential concentration in quantum kernels similarly limits their utility. Understanding their relationship is crucial for developing practical quantum machine learning.
method: The authors construct a nonparametric quantum kernel from a parametrized quantum neural network and prove that the concentration of the kernel's feature map is directly tied to the variance of the cost function, thereby connecting the two phenomena.
result: They rigorously show that exponential concentration in quantum kernels occurs if and only if the corresponding variational circuit exhibits barren plateaus, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: This equivalence implies that techniques to mitigate barren plateaus can also address kernel concentration, and vice versa, guiding the design of quantum machine learning models.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper bridges the gap between experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations in the saturated regime and complexity-theoretic foundations previously limited to the dilute regime, providing new hardness results for BosonSampling with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity-theoretic justifications only apply to the dilute regime. This disconnect undermines the theoretical basis for these experiments.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic techniques to analyze BosonSampling in the saturated regime, likely involving approximate counting and hardness arguments adapted to linear optical networks with many photons per mode.
result: They establish computational hardness results for BosonSampling with a linear number of modes, showing that sampling from the output distribution is classically hard under plausible conjectures, thus validating the quantum advantage in this regime.
conclusion: The work provides a solid theoretical foundation for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, extending the complexity-theoretic framework to the practically relevant saturated regime.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational hardness, but its robustness to noise is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with projective measurements and local noise, using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior.
result: They find that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.
conclusion: The results highlight the fragility of measurement-induced entanglement to noise, which is crucial for practical quantum information processing and complexity.

title: Quantum Non-Markovian Hatano-Nelson Model
authors: Sumit Kumar Jana, Ryo Hanai, Tan van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa, And Archak Purkayastha
abstract:
Author(s): Sumit Kumar Jana, Ryo Hanai, Tan Van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa, and Archak Purkayastha

While considering non-Hermitian Hamiltonians arising in the presence of dissipation, in most cases, the dissipation is taken to be frequency-independent. However, this idealization may not always be applicable in experimental settings, where dissipation can be frequency-dependent. Such frequency-dep…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070404] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson model with frequency-dependent dissipation, revealing non-Markovian effects and their impact on quantum transport and thermodynamics.
motivation: Most studies of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians assume frequency-independent dissipation, which is unrealistic in experiments. The authors aim to incorporate frequency-dependent dissipation to capture non-Markovian behavior.
method: They introduce a non-Markovian Hatano-Nelson model with frequency-dependent dissipation, analyze its spectral properties and transport, and derive thermodynamic implications using Green's functions and master equation approaches.
result: They find that non-Markovian dissipation leads to novel localization and transport phenomena, and modifies thermodynamic quantities such as heat currents and entropy production.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of non-Markovian effects in non-Hermitian quantum systems and provides a framework for studying thermodynamics in such settings.

title: Emergent Decoherence Dynamics In Doubly Disordered Spin Networks

Elucidating the emergence of irreversible macroscopic laws from reversible quantum many-body dynamics remains challenging, particularly in disordered media. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070803] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies emergent decoherence dynamics in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, revealing a universal decoherence law.
motivation: Understanding how irreversible macroscopic laws emerge from reversible quantum many-body dynamics, especially in disordered media, is a fundamental challenge.
method: The authors experimentally investigate a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, likely using dynamical decoupling or similar techniques to probe decoherence.
result: They uncover an emergent decoherence law for 13C nuclear spins, possibly showing universal scaling or a specific functional form.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into decoherence in disordered spin systems, with implications for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Joint Parameter Estimation And Multidimensional Reconciliation For Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Jisheng Dai, Xue-Qin Jiang, Peng Huang, Tao Wang, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Jisheng Dai, Xue-Qin Jiang, Peng Huang, Tao Wang, and Guihua Zeng

Accurate quantum channel parameter estimation is essential for effective information reconciliation in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD). However, conventional maximum likelihood (ML) estimators rely on a large amount of disclosed data, leading to a significant loss in symbol eff…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022429] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a joint parameter estimation and multidimensional reconciliation method for CV-QKD to reduce symbol loss and improve key rate.
motivation: Conventional ML estimators for CV-QKD require large disclosed data, causing significant symbol loss. The authors aim to improve efficiency by jointly estimating parameters and performing reconciliation.
method: They develop a joint estimation and reconciliation scheme that integrates parameter estimation with multidimensional reconciliation, likely using a modified ML approach or iterative algorithm.
result: The method reduces the amount of disclosed data needed for parameter estimation, thereby increasing the effective symbol rate and key rate in CV-QKD.
conclusion: The proposed joint approach enhances the performance of CV-QKD systems by mitigating the overhead of parameter estimation, making them more practical.

title: Directional Charging Of Topological Quantum Energy-storage Devices Driven By The non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, And Hongrong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, and Hongrong Li

The skin effect is a phenomenon characterized by the exponential localization of wave functions at a boundary in non-Hermitian topological systems, demonstrating potential applications in the field of quantum information. Here we explore its application in optimizing the performance of quantum energ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023712] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using the non-Hermitian skin effect to directionally charge quantum energy storage devices, enhancing charging efficiency.
motivation: Quantum energy storage is a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and improving charging performance is crucial. The non-Hermitian skin effect offers a novel mechanism for directional energy transfer.
method: The authors theoretically model a quantum battery coupled to a non-Hermitian system exhibiting the skin effect, analyzing how the directional localization of modes can be harnessed for charging.
result: They find that the skin effect enables faster and more efficient charging compared to conventional setups, with the direction of charging controllable by system parameters.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a promising application of non-Hermitian topology in quantum thermodynamics, potentially advancing practical quantum energy storage.

title: $\mathit{In}$ situ Rewiring Of Two-dimensional Ion Lattice Interactions Using Metastable State Shelving
authors: Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, And Philip Richerme
abstract:

Trapped-ion lattice geometries, which determine the interactions between trapped-ion qubits, are typically governed by the balance of Coulomb repulsion forces with the external trapping potential. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 022425] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates in-situ rewiring of trapped-ion lattice interactions using metastable state shelving, enabling dynamic control of qubit-qubit couplings.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum simulators typically have fixed lattice geometries, limiting their flexibility. The authors aim to dynamically control ion interactions to enable more versatile quantum simulations.
method: They use metastable state shelving to selectively alter the effective trapping potential for certain ions, thereby changing the lattice geometry and the resulting spin-spin interactions.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the ability to rewire the ion lattice and modify qubit-qubit interactions in a controlled manner.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for dynamically programming trapped-ion quantum simulators, expanding their capabilities for studying quantum many-body physics.

title: Frequency Shifts Heralding Ground-state Squeezing And Entanglement Of Two Coupled Harmonic Oscillators
authors: Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, and Karol Gietka

It is often argued that two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, even when cooled to their ground state, display no inherently quantum features beyond quantized energy levels. Here, we challenge this view by showing that their classical observables encode genuinely quantum features. In par…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022426] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that two coupled quantum harmonic oscillators in their ground state exhibit quantum features in classical observables, specifically frequency shifts that herald ground-state squeezing and entanglement.
motivation: It challenges the common belief that coupled harmonic oscillators in the ground state have no quantum features beyond quantized energy levels, aiming to reveal genuine quantum properties in classical observables.
method: The authors analyze two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, deriving frequency shifts and relating them to ground-state squeezing and entanglement measures.
result: They find that frequency shifts in the classical observables can indicate the presence of quantum squeezing and entanglement in the ground state.
conclusion: The work provides a new way to detect quantum features in harmonic oscillator systems via frequency shifts, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Agnostic Parameter Estimation With Large Spins
authors: Huining Zhang And X. X. Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Huining Zhang and X. X. Yi

The quantum Fisher information of a quantum state with respect to a certain parameter quantifies the sensitivity of the quantum state to changes in that parameter. Maximizing the quantum Fisher information is essential for achieving the optimal estimation precision of quantum sensors. A typical quan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022612] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies agnostic parameter estimation with large spins, focusing on maximizing quantum Fisher information without prior knowledge of the probe state.
motivation: Quantum sensors require optimal estimation precision, which depends on maximizing quantum Fisher information. However, in practice, the probe state may be unknown or noisy, so agnostic estimation is important.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Fisher information for large spin systems and propose strategies to optimize estimation precision in an agnostic setting, likely using spin coherent states or other large-spin states.
result: They derive bounds or conditions for achieving optimal precision and demonstrate the performance of their approach with examples.
conclusion: The work provides insights into robust quantum metrology with large spins, contributing to the theory of quantum parameter estimation.

title: Robust Two-qubit Gates For Semiconductor Spin Qubits Based On Dynamical Dimensionality Reduction
authors: Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, And Zheng-Yuan Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, and Zheng-Yuan Xue

High-fidelity two-qubit gates leverage qubit-qubit interactions and are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, environmental noise and imperfect control of the interactions are inevitable, which degrade the quality of gate operations. Here we introduce local microwave driving in conven…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022613] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a robust two-qubit gate scheme for semiconductor spin qubits using local microwave driving and dynamical dimensionality reduction to suppress noise and imperfect interactions.
motivation: High-fidelity two-qubit gates are essential for scalable quantum computation, but environmental noise and imperfect control degrade gate quality. The authors aim to improve gate robustness in semiconductor spin qubit platforms.
method: They introduce local microwave driving in a conventional two-qubit gate setup and apply dynamical dimensionality reduction to design control pulses that are resilient to noise and interaction errors.
result: The proposed scheme achieves high-fidelity two-qubit gates with significantly improved robustness against common noise sources, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to enhance two-qubit gate performance in semiconductor spin qubits, contributing to the development of scalable quantum processors.

title: Tabletop Reversibility Of Phase-covariant Operations
authors: Fangzhen Chen And Xueyuan Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Fangzhen Chen and Xueyuan Hu

Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are both fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and it is of great importance to study the interplay between them. In this paper, we study tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant quantum operations and obtain sharply different conclusions for fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022419] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies tabletop reversibility of phase-covariant quantum operations, revealing a sharp contrast between finite and infinite dimensions.
motivation: Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and understanding their interplay is important.
method: The authors analyze tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant operations, deriving conditions for reversibility in finite and infinite dimensions.
result: They find that TTR holds for all phase-covariant operations in finite dimensions but fails in infinite dimensions, with specific counterexamples.
conclusion: The results highlight the role of dimension in reversibility of quantum operations, contributing to the theory of quantum information and open systems.

title: Quantum Coherence And Entanglement In Wireless Quantum Batteries
authors: Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, and Dong Wang

We investigate the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system mediated by a common structured bosonic environment. By employing a unified resource-theoretic analysis, we elucidate the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022420] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of wireless quantum batteries in a common structured bosonic environment, using resource-theoretic analysis to reveal the roles of non-Markovian memory and coupling symmetry.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and understanding how environmental memory and symmetry affect their performance is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors employ a unified resource-theoretic analysis to investigate the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system mediated by a common structured bosonic environment.
result: They elucidate the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in the charging process and thermodynamic efficiency.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into optimizing quantum battery performance by leveraging environmental memory and symmetry, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Giant-atom Quantum Battery
authors: Lei Qiao And P. Z. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Qiao and P. Z. Zhao

Most studies of quantum batteries have been restricted to conventional atoms whose size is much smaller than the electromagnetic modes. Here we propose a scheme for a quantum battery based on giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide. Specifically, both the charger and the battery are giant atoms…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022205] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum battery scheme using giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide, exploring energy storage and transfer in a quantum thermodynamic context.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and most studies use conventional atoms. This work aims to exploit giant atoms' unique coupling properties to improve battery performance.
method: The authors design a quantum battery where both charger and battery are giant atoms coupled to a common waveguide, and analyze the charging dynamics and energy storage using quantum master equations.
result: They find that giant-atom quantum batteries can achieve faster charging and higher stored energy compared to conventional setups, due to the interference effects from multiple coupling points.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom quantum battery offers a promising platform for quantum energy storage, with potential advantages in charging speed and capacity.

title: Theory Of The Uhlmann Phase In quasi-Hermitian Quantum Systems
authors: Xu-Yang Hou, Xin Wang, And Hao Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Xu-Yang Hou, Xin Wang, and Hao Guo

Geometric phases play a fundamental role in understanding the geometric structure of quantum states, yet extending the Uhlmann phase to non-Hermitian systems poses significant challenges due to parameter-dependent inner product structures. In this work, we develop a comprehensive theory of the Uhlma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084106] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of the Uhlmann phase for quasi-Hermitian quantum systems, addressing the challenge of parameter-dependent inner products.
motivation: Extending geometric phases to non-Hermitian systems is challenging due to the parameter-dependent inner product structure, and a complete theory of the Uhlmann phase in such systems is lacking.
method: The authors formulate the Uhlmann phase for quasi-Hermitian systems by appropriately handling the metric operator and the parallel transport condition, providing a systematic framework.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the Uhlmann phase and its holonomy, and demonstrate its properties with examples, showing consistency with the Hermitian limit.
conclusion: The work establishes a solid theoretical foundation for the Uhlmann phase in quasi-Hermitian systems, which may have implications for understanding geometric phases in non-Hermitian quantum information contexts.

title: Engineering Quantum Mpemba Effect By Liouvillian Skin Effect
authors: Xiang Zhang, Chen Sun, And Fuxiang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Zhang, Chen Sun, and Fuxiang Li

We propose an approach to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—wherein an initial state farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one—using the Liouvillian skin effect (LSE) in open quantum systems. In an open quantum chain with LSE, we show that the QME can be readily achieved simpl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084305] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect using the Liouvillian skin effect in open quantum systems.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect, where a state farther from equilibrium relaxes faster, is a counterintuitive phenomenon with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control. The authors aim to provide a systematic way to realize it.
method: They consider an open quantum chain with the Liouvillian skin effect, which leads to non-reciprocal hopping and localization of eigenmodes. They show that this effect can be used to engineer the relaxation dynamics to exhibit the QME.
result: They demonstrate that the QME can be readily achieved in such systems, and analyze the conditions and mechanisms behind it.
conclusion: The Liouvillian skin effect provides a versatile tool for engineering the quantum Mpemba effect, offering new insights into relaxation processes in open quantum systems.

title: Defect In Diamond With Millisecond-scale Spin Relaxation Time At Room Temperature
authors: Sounak Mukherjee, Anran Li, Johannes Eberle, Sean Karg, Zi-Huai Zhang, Mayer M. Feldman, Yilin Chen, Mark E. Turiansky, Mengen Wang, Yogendra Limbu, Tharnier O. Puel, Yueguang Shi, Matthew L. Markham, Rajesh L. Patel, Patryk Gumann, Michael E. Flatté, Chris G. van de Walle, Stephen A. Lyon, And Nathalie P. de Leon
abstract:
Author(s): Sounak Mukherjee, Anran Li, Johannes Eberle, Sean Karg, Zi-Huai Zhang, Mayer M. Feldman, Yilin Chen, Mark E. Turiansky, Mengen Wang, Yogendra Limbu, Tharnier O. Puel, Yueguang Shi, Matthew L. Markham, Rajesh L. Patel, Patryk Gumann, Michael E. Flatté, Chris G. Van de Walle, Stephen A. Lyon, and Nathalie P. de Leon

Nitrogen-vacancy centers and substitutional nitrogen (P1 centers) in diamond have until now been the only solid-state electron spin defects known to reach millisecond spin relaxation times (T
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074105] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a new defect in diamond (WAR5) with millisecond-scale spin relaxation time at room temperature, potentially useful for quantum sensing and networking.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin defects with long coherence times for quantum applications, as only NV and P1 centers were previously known to have millisecond T1 at room temperature.
method: The authors characterize the spin dynamics and optical spin polarization of the WAR5 defect using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, hypothesizing it to be the neutral oxygen vacancy center.
result: The WAR5 defect exhibits a T1 of ~1 ms at room temperature, rising to ~14 minutes at 4 K, making it one of the longest-lived spin defects in solids.
conclusion: The discovery of a new long-lived spin defect in diamond expands the toolkit for quantum technologies, potentially enabling new applications in sensing and quantum networking.

title: Control-driven Critical Fluctuations Across Quantum Trajectories
authors: Haining Pan, Thomas Iadecola, E. M. Stoudenmire, And J. H. Pixley
abstract:
Author(s): Haining Pan, Thomas Iadecola, E. M. Stoudenmire, and J. H. Pixley

Monitored quantum circuits in which entangling unitary dynamics compete with projective local measurements can host measurement-induced phase transitions witnessed by entanglement measures at late times. Adding feedback conditioned on the measurement outcomes gives rise to another type of phase tran…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074307] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-induced phase transitions in monitored quantum circuits with feedback, focusing on control-driven critical fluctuations across quantum trajectories.
motivation: To understand how feedback control affects critical phenomena in monitored quantum systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with feedback using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, likely employing tensor network methods.
result: They find that feedback can drive new types of phase transitions and critical fluctuations, extending the understanding of measurement-induced transitions.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of control in quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Dynamics With Stationary Thermal States
authors: Adrián A. Budini
abstract:
Author(s): Adrián A. Budini

Quantum and classical systems can consistently be coupled via nonunitary time-irreversible mechanisms. In this paper, we characterize which kind of corresponding dynamics converge in the stationary regime to a thermal hybrid state, that is, a density matrix that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024125] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes hybrid quantum-classical dynamics that converge to thermal stationary states, linking nonunitary couplings to entropy maximization.
motivation: To understand how quantum and classical systems can be consistently coupled and to identify conditions under which such hybrid dynamics reach thermal equilibrium.
method: The author analyzes nonunitary time-irreversible coupling mechanisms and derives conditions for the stationary state to be a thermal hybrid state that maximizes hybrid arrangement entropy.
result: The paper provides a characterization of dynamics that lead to thermal hybrid states, extending thermodynamic concepts to hybrid quantum-classical settings.
conclusion: The findings offer a framework for studying thermodynamics in hybrid systems, potentially relevant for quantum thermal machines and information thermodynamics.

title: Geometry-driven Thermodynamic Anomaly In Overdamped Langevin Dynamics
authors: Sehyeok Lee And Min Soo Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Sehyeok Lee and Min Soo Kim

Changing geometry creates its own overdamped thermodynamic anomaly. This is the geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped anomaly known for Langevin systems in nonuniform or time-dependent temperature fields. We show this for Langevin dynamics in [MATH] under a time-dependent potent…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024118] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped thermodynamic anomaly in overdamped Langevin dynamics with time-dependent potentials, showing that changing geometry itself induces anomalous thermodynamic behavior.
motivation: To understand how geometric changes affect thermodynamic properties in stochastic systems, extending known anomalies from temperature fields to geometry.
method: The authors analyze overdamped Langevin dynamics under a time-dependent potential, deriving expressions for thermodynamic quantities and identifying conditions for anomalous behavior linked to geometric changes.
result: They demonstrate that geometry-driven changes produce an overdamped thermodynamic anomaly analogous to the underdamped-overdamped anomaly, with implications for work and heat fluctuations.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of geometry in stochastic thermodynamics, offering new insights into non-equilibrium processes and potential applications in small-scale engines.

title: Counting Observables In Stochastic Excursions
authors: Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:

Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields of research, from quantum thermal machines to biological motors. We introduce a framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories, dubbed stochastic excursions, of pr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022102] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for analyzing the statistics of counting observables in stochastic excursions, with applications to quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields, including quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories (stochastic excursions) of stochastic processes.
result: The framework provides a way to compute statistics of counting observables in stochastic excursions, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The framework offers a new tool for studying fluctuations in stochastic processes, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and other fields.

title: Thermalization Rates And Quantum Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances: Insights From Operator Hydrodynamics
authors: Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, And Curt von Keyserlingk
abstract:
Author(s): Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, and Curt von Keyserlingk

In thermalizing many-body quantum systems without conservation laws, such as ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, local expectation values are predicted to decay to their equilibrium values exponentially quickly. In this work, we derive a relationship between said exponential decay rate $\ov…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033186] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a relationship between exponential thermalization rates and quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances using operator hydrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the timescales of thermalization in many-body quantum systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors use operator hydrodynamics to analyze ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, deriving a formula connecting decay rates to resonances.
result: They establish a quantitative link between thermalization rates and quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances, providing a new tool for predicting relaxation dynamics.
conclusion: This work advances the theoretical framework for non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, offering insights into the physical constraints on information processing.

title: Generalized Cross-resonance Scheme For Maximally Entangling Two-qutrit Gates
authors: Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, And Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, and Ray-Kuang Lee

The cross-resonance scheme is extended to multilevel quantum systems, enabling direct entangling operations on the 1–2 levels of fixed-frequency transmon qutrits. Numerical simulations demonstrate parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space and prepare high-fidelity Bell state.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032023] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the cross-resonance scheme to transmon qutrits, enabling direct entangling two-qutrit gates and high-fidelity Bell state preparation.
motivation: To enable direct entangling operations on multilevel quantum systems, specifically fixed-frequency transmon qutrits, which could improve quantum computing efficiency.
method: The authors generalize the cross-resonance scheme to qutrits and use numerical simulations to demonstrate parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space.
result: The simulations show that the proposed gates can prepare high-fidelity Bell states, indicating the scheme's effectiveness.
conclusion: The generalized cross-resonance scheme provides a viable method for entangling qutrits, potentially advancing quantum computing with multilevel systems.

title: Intermodal Entanglement In A Quantum Optical Model Of High-harmonic Generation Due To The Backaction On The Driving Field
authors: Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, And Tamás Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, and Tamás Kiss

Preparation of nonclassical light with special quantum properties is essential for quantum technologies. High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a process that not only enables the creation of attosecond pulses but also has the potential to generate light with intricate quantum properties. In a recent exp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033154] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies intermodal entanglement in high-harmonic generation, showing that the backaction on the driving field can produce nonclassical correlations between harmonic modes.
motivation: High-harmonic generation is a promising source of nonclassical light for quantum technologies, and understanding its quantum properties is essential. The backaction on the driving field may enable entanglement generation, which has not been fully explored.
method: The authors analyze a quantum optical model of HHG, treating the driving field quantum mechanically and deriving the state of the harmonic modes. They compute entanglement measures such as logarithmic negativity and quantum mutual information between different harmonic modes.
result: They find that intermodal entanglement can be generated between different harmonic modes due to the backaction, with the degree of entanglement depending on parameters like the driving field intensity and the number of harmonics.
conclusion: The results suggest that HHG can serve as a source of entangled multi-mode light, which could be useful for quantum information processing and quantum communication.

title: Controlling Emergent Dynamical Behavior Via Phase-engineered Strong Symmetries
authors: Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, And Parvinder Solanki
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, and Parvinder Solanki

Symmetry constraints provide a powerful means to control the dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the set of accessible control parameters is often limited. Here, we show that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces a phase-dependent strong symmet…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033166] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces phase-dependent strong symmetries, enabling control of emergent dynamical behavior.
motivation: Symmetry constraints are powerful for controlling open quantum systems, but accessible control parameters are often limited. The authors aim to expand control by exploiting a tunable phase in the coupling.
method: They analyze a cavity QED system with a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling, showing that this phase induces strong symmetries that depend on the phase. They likely use theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting dynamics.
result: The phase-dependent strong symmetries allow for control of emergent dynamical behavior, such as steady-state selection or suppression of certain decay channels.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for controlling open quantum systems via phase-engineered symmetries, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Classical Optimization Of Reduced Density Matrix Estimations With Classical Shadows Using $N$-representability Conditions Under Shot Noise Considerations
authors: Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, And Michael Streif
abstract:
Author(s): Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, and Michael Streif

Classical shadow tomography has become a powerful tool in learning about quantum states prepared on a quantum computer. Recent works have used classical shadows to variationally enforce [MATH]-representability conditions on the two-particle reduced density matrix. In this paper, we build upon previous …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033167] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes classical shadow tomography for estimating two-particle reduced density matrices by enforcing N-representability conditions, improving accuracy under shot noise.
motivation: Classical shadow tomography is a powerful tool for learning quantum states, but estimating reduced density matrices (RDMs) can be inefficient. Enforcing N-representability conditions can improve accuracy, but previous methods were not optimized for shot noise.
method: The authors formulate a classical optimization problem that incorporates N-representability constraints on the two-particle RDM estimated from classical shadows, and solve it under shot noise considerations.
result: The optimized estimation reduces the required number of shots and improves the accuracy of RDM estimates compared to standard shadow tomography, especially in the presence of noise.
conclusion: The proposed method enhances the practicality of classical shadow tomography for quantum chemistry and other applications requiring accurate RDM estimates.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to analyze out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model, linking system-bath interactions to random matrix structures.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems is crucial; OTOCs are key probes, and free probability offers a new analytical tool.
method: The authors map a quantum circuit with system-bath interactions to free probability structures, deriving analytical expressions for OTOCs.
result: They characterize OTOC growth and saturation, showing universal behavior governed by free probability, and connect to random matrix theory.
conclusion: The work provides a new framework for analyzing quantum circuits, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and chaos.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding universal signatures of quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, a key diagnostic of quantum chaos, for chaotic many-body systems, extending results to all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain leading and beyond-leading-order contributions to the spectral form factor, revealing universal behavior dependent on symmetry class.
conclusion: The results deepen our understanding of quantum chaos and its connection to thermodynamics, providing a benchmark for numerical and experimental studies.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel method to detect quantum dot charging energies by probing nuclear spin magnetism, relevant to spin qubit platforms.
motivation: Understanding charging energies in quantum dots is crucial for spin qubit operation, but existing detection methods may be limited. The authors propose a new strategy exploiting nuclear spin response.
method: They experimentally probe the nuclear spin magnetism in few-electron quantum dots and correlate its response with charging events.
result: The method successfully detects charging energies, demonstrating a new tool for characterizing quantum dot devices.
conclusion: This approach offers a non-invasive way to probe quantum dot properties, potentially aiding in the development of spin-based quantum computing.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for simulating quantum systems using Pauli propagation, including theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Efficient simulation of quantum systems is crucial for understanding and developing quantum technologies, and Pauli propagation offers a promising approach.
method: The authors develop a computational framework based on propagating Pauli operators through quantum circuits, providing a unified formalism for simulation.
result: The framework is implemented in software and demonstrated on various applications, showing its utility for quantum simulation tasks.
conclusion: Pauli propagation provides a versatile and efficient tool for simulating quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum information and beyond.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, degrading performance. Adaptive estimation of these rates can enhance decoding.
method: The authors propose a sliding-window approach to estimate time-varying error rates from syndrome data, and integrate these estimates into the decoder.
result: The method reconstructs drifting error rates and demonstrates improved decoder performance compared to static estimation.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is beneficial for practical quantum error correction, offering a way to handle non-stationary noise.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and manipulate electrons on a neon surface, and analyze its feasibility and tunability.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, offering a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The work identifies a promising direction for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental validation is needed.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
